title: SQRTPI 30 of 30 - the sentence scores powf against pow, not SQRTPI calls

upstream_anchor.section: XMD-003 - SQRTPI computed via pow, not correctly-rounded sqrt

status_plain: Excel computes SQRTPI as (n*pi)^0.5 through its pow routine, which is not correctly-rounded: it agrees with a correctly-rounded sqrt at normal magnitudes but is 1 ULP off at scattered points near overflow. The source names the exact witness - at the input where n*pi equals f64::MAX, correctly-rounded sqrt gives 0x5fefffffffffffff and Excel's pow gives 0x5ff0000000000000, one ULP high, and Excel is the LESS accurate of the two. This is explicitly not an x87 effect; 64-bit Excel and Rust are both SSE2. OxFunc reproduces it by using (n*pi).powf(0.5). The figure "30/30 sampled inputs" is real and the build (16.0 build 20026) is stated two lines later - but the sentence's grammatical subject is Rust's powf reproducing Excel's pow, not SQRTPI. Whether the 30 inputs were SQRTPI worksheet calls or direct pow probes is not resolvable from the text, so this record flags the attribution rather than publishing a clean SQRTPI pass rate.
